reportWin: A win. Please enjoy it responsibly.

The {o} hung around to shake hands. Sportsmanship, or they could not find the bus keys.
Coach says "we found a way." The way involved blocking, which is new.
Somebody already painted the score on a barn outside town. Dry by morning, they swear.
reportLoss: Fans left muttering. A few left muttering encouragement.
The team looked tired. The fans looked tired. The hot dogs looked fine.
A loud fan asked for a refund. The ticket was free. We refunded it anyway.
The band played us out. Pity may have been involved.
The coach says it was close. The scoreboard politely disagrees.
Fans bought snacks to cope. Consider it emotional-support revenue.
The parking lot emptied at the half. The concession stand did not.
The {t} had their chances. The chances left town with the {o}.
A kid asked if we get a do-over. We do not. We checked the rulebook.
The film session is going to be long. The film session is always long after this kind of game.
Somebody booed. Somebody else shushed them. Both had a point.
We were in it until we were not. That is the official summary.
The {o} made the simple plays. We made the interesting ones. The interesting ones did not work.
reportLossBig: The visiting fans were louder than ours. Ours were in the parking lot.
A kid asked if we were the other team's practice squad. We are not. We checked.
The final score has been sealed in a box and buried behind the stadium.
Several fans left in the third quarter and took the good seat cushions.
Some fans depression was cured taking comfort in how bad we are.
We should keep our day jobs.

The scoreboard operator asked if he could just write "a lot" on our side. Denied.
Our mascot sat down. The {o} mascot brought him water.
Talk radio will be unkind. Talk radio is already unkind. This will not help.
The bus ride home is going to be quiet, except for the one guy who always talks.

reportTie: Nobody won. Nobody lost. A kid in section C asked for a refund on the feeling.
A tie is like kissing your cousin. Nobody is sure how to feel.

The {t} and the {o} played to a draw. The parking lot argument will go to extra time.
Both teams left with half a win and a full headache.
The band started the fight song, stopped, started the sad song, stopped, packed up.
A tie. The league office loves a tie. Nobody else does.
We could have won. They could have won. The football chose neither.
Overtime was available. Dignity was not. We shook hands at even.
The coin for overtime is still in somebody's pocket. We will not speak of it.
reportLosing: The concession stand ran out of napkins, then ran out of excuses.
Money out is bigger than money in. The accountant has taken up a hobby: sighing.
A loss on the books this week. Please do not look at the books.
Net negative. The accountant would like a word, and a snack.
In the red this week. The pens in the front office are being rationed.
Our tax write-offs are going to be lit this year.
The till is lighter than the crowd. That is not the direction we wanted.
We paid more to put on a game than the game paid us. The irony is not deductible.
Cash went out. The crowd did not quite come in. Math is undefeated.
The books are frowning. The books have a very expressive font this week.
A week like this is why the safe has a combination and a prayer.
If enthusiasm were revenue we would be fine. Enthusiasm is not revenue.
reportAway: Road trip. Somebody left the film reels on the bus.

We traveled four hours to be booed by strangers. Character building.
Gas, tolls, and one very expensive diner. Road life.

The {o} crowd brought signs. One of them was spelled correctly.

The visiting locker room smelled like a wet dog and old tape. Home field, they call it.
Four hours out, four hours back, and a diner coffee that could strip paint.
Somebody packed the wrong helmet bag. We made do. We always make do on the road.
The {t} traveled well. The expense report traveled better, unfortunately.
